verdict.headline: Long Treasury yields close at a 24-year high on hot service prices as the Nasdaq sets a record
verdict.label: Close Mon: S&P 500 7,773.95 (+0.66%), Nasdaq 27,477.31 (+1.05%, record), Dow +0.18%; VIX 16.21 (+0.90); 30Y ~5.661% (above 2002 high 5.644%; intraday 5.703%), 10Y ~5.307% (intraday 5.349%); DXY ~102.27; WTI ~$89; NVDA $238.90 record.
verdict.rationale_short:
What happened: the ISM services prices index rose to 74.0, its highest since July 2022 and above a 72.9 forecast, and services employment returned to 50.1. The thirty-year Treasury yield reached 5.703% and the ten-year 5.349% intraday, the highest since 2002, before closing near 5.661% and 5.307%, each up about 3 basis points. The thirty-year close is above the 5.644% 2002 high this report has used as its line for renewed long-bond pressure. Stocks did not follow: the Nasdaq rose 1.05% to a record and Nvidia closed at a record $238.90, while the Dow gained only 0.18% and the VIX rose 0.90 points. The dollar index held above 102 at about 102.27 on the euro's slide.

What it means: long yields rose for a second session without help from the Fed path, with October hike odds near 19%. Either investors want more yield to hold long bonds regardless of the Fed, which a narrow, technology-led stock rally has not priced, or the long end is repricing inflation while growth holds, which stocks can carry. One session does not separate them; this week's three-, ten- and thirty-year auctions and Wednesday's Fed minutes are the next evidence.

What would change the picture: a thirty-year close back under 5.644% would say Monday's break did not hold; a ten-year close above 5.349% with the Nasdaq lower would show higher yields reaching the market's leaders, and an S&P 500 close under 7,666.45 would show the index following. Note: news sites could not be opened from this run, so figures rest on search summaries of the cited sources.
verdict.lede_short: The thirty-year Treasury yield closed above its 2002 high after service-sector prices rose at the fastest pace since 2022, yet the Nasdaq and Nvidia closed at records. Long yields are rising while Fed hike odds stay near 19%, so the pressure is coming from inflation or bond supply rather than the Fed. This week's ten- and thirty-year auctions decide which; a thirty-year back under 5.644% would undo Monday's break.

supporting_data.label: The ISM services prices index rose 1.4 points to 74.0, the highest since July 2022, against a 72.9 forecast, while employment returned to 50.1 — service prices are rising with factory prices, and hiring in services stopped shrinking.

The thirty-year yield closed near 5.661% and the ten-year near 5.307%, after intraday highs of 5.703% and 5.349%, the highest since 2002 — the thirty-year close is above its 5.644% 2002 high for the first time.
The Nasdaq rose 1.05% to a record 27,477.31 and Nvidia 2.1% to a record $238.90, a $5.76 trillion value — stocks priced steady Fed odds and set aside 24-year highs in long yields.
The dollar index rose 0.33% to about 102.27 after touching 102.53, its highest since April 2025 — the euro's slide on Spanish and French political risk kept the dollar above 102 all session.
October hike odds stood near 19% on CME FedWatch on Monday morning, against about 64% two weeks earlier — long yields rose without help from the expected Fed path.

Intel fell about 4% after Elon Musk confirmed talks with TSMC about joining his Terafab chip venture, where Intel had been the only named partner — the first sign Intel's foundry role there could be shared.

Rose 1.48% to $525.18 after a Melius Research upgrade citing demand for AI security and governance products.
Rose 1.90% to $741.90 as part of the large-technology rally that took the Nasdaq to a record.
US shares rose about 2% after Elon Musk confirmed talks about TSMC joining the Terafab venture; TSMC has not commented and Musk called them just discussions.

trade_setups.thesis: The thirty-year closed near 5.661%, above its 5.644% 2002 high for the first time, after the ISM services prices index hit 74.0, with October hike odds near 19%; three Treasury auctions this week test whether demand for long bonds holds at these yields.
trade_setups.entry: Thirty-year ~5.661% between Monday's 5.703% intraday high above and the 5.644% 2002 high below.
trade_setups.invalidation: A close back under 5.644% by Friday would say the break did not hold; a close above 5.703%, especially after a weak thirty-year auction on Thursday, would extend it.
trade_setups.horizon: October 6-9, through the auctions and Fed minutes

trade_setups.asset: Nasdaq and Nvidia against the ten-year
trade_setups.thesis: The Nasdaq and Nvidia set records with the ten-year at 5.307%, 4 basis points under its intraday high, in a narrow rally: the Dow rose 0.18% and the VIX rose 0.90 points on the up day.
trade_setups.invalidation: A ten-year close above 5.349% with the Nasdaq lower would show the discount rate reaching the leaders; an S&P 500 close under 7,666.45 would show the index following; continued records with the ten-year steady would say stocks are carrying the yield level.

trade_setups.thesis: The dollar index closed near 102.27 after a 102.53 high, the highest since April 2025, driven by the euro's slide on Spanish and French political risk rather than by US rates.
trade_setups.invalidation: A close back under 102 would mark Monday as a reaction to Spain's election call; Fed minutes on Wednesday showing several officials open to more hikes would add a rate reason to the euro reason.
